reference_producer.scope: Source control, not an installed-client receipt or a reusable database dump.

synthetic_legacy_shape.scope: Transform a stopped, disposable copy of real current-producer API admissions. This is not a physical pre-upgrade rehearsal.
preconditions: Database belongs to the test cohort; no production input.
Server is stopped; use a disposable copy.
Selected command_id, command_type, workflow_instance_id and workflow_run_id equal the original API receipt.
Stored request_id equals the original caller key token and exactly one dw_command_intents row belongs to command_id.
synthetic_legacy_shape.transaction: BEGIN IMMEDIATE; verify preconditions before mutations; require one affected row from each statement; COMMIT only if all succeed, otherwise ROLLBACK.
statements: UPDATE workflow_commands SET request_id=:legacy_request_id WHERE id=:command_id
synthetic_legacy_shape.preserve: Every other command column, related update/signal, task, history and payload-registry row remains byte-for-byte unchanged.

legacy_readback.explicit_original_run: Read back the original receipt, including after continuation; do not claim the successor was targeted.

ambiguity.setup: Admit original under token-key. Admit a second command under second-key; transform only that second command to raw token-key.
Admit under token-key; transform that command to raw keys.tokens[type], removing its intent.
Keep the original modern admission under token-key unchanged.

case_only.setup: Admit under CaseSensitive, then transform that command to raw CaseSensitive. Exact-byte retry reads back unverified.

baseline_key_authority.update: Published 3.8 API admissions retain the raw caller request_id. These are physical legacy-key upgrade seeds.
baseline_key_authority.signal: Published 3.8 ordinary signal rows have request_id NULL; only bridge identities are stored. They are unkeyed controls, not physical retained caller-key proof. Do not manufacture a raw signal key or infer equality.

physical_upgrade.scope: Separate actual old-image admission and schema-upgrade cell. Do not substitute the synthetic transform or minimal orphan command-row schema tests.
procedure: Admit real signal/update receipts through baseline public APIs; record exact keys, command/run/update identities and rows/history. Use the baseline advertised worker protocol; seed generation is not a current-SDK acceptance claim.
Stop all baseline Servers, keep the database and backup, and record the baseline image/source and database fingerprints.
Run the exact candidate image schema-upgrade once; require the declared schema transition and an empty dw_command_intents table.
Prove original raw request_id values and command/history rows were preserved, then start the exact candidate image.

Perform legacy readbacks and name/target conflicts; compare full rows/history and original identities. Keep synthetic ambiguity cells separate unless their seed was genuinely created through the baseline API.
physical_upgrade.no_inference: The 3.9.1 source tests prove all-backend row preservation separately. They do not prove this installed upgrade cell for an SDK.

postcommit_response_loss.scope: Separate real admission cell. A proxy must establish that the Server committed before dropping the response; then retry the original key. Synthetic legacy setup does not establish response-loss evidence.

receipt_requirements: Exact fixture Git commit/blob and digest
Actual SDK/CLI package and Server source/index/platform identities
Synthetic-shape versus physical-upgrade versus postcommit-loss cell label
Original and returned command/run/update identities and complete zero-write snapshots where required
Nonpass and cleanup outcomes; no inferred PASS from source lineage
